# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37 (Bu-Vb Pc37)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc37
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37
**Title (English, from literature):** Eating at the wrong time
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-pc37

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37, titled *Vikālabhojana* ("Eating at the wrong time"), establishes that a monk who consumes solid or soft food between noon and dawn commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. According to the Vibhaṅga, the prohibition was laid down at Rājagaha to forbid eating during the improper period (*vikāla*) [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983]. Under standard monastic discipline, the allowable period for taking meals was restricted to the hours from sunrise until midday [Wijayaratna 1990].
This training rule is central to accounts of the Second Buddhist Council [Bapat 1956; Hazra 2002; Sarao & Long 2017]. The Vajjian monks claimed as allowable the *dvaṅgulakappa*—the practice of consuming food past midday when the shadow was within two finger-breadths or digits wide—which the council ruled unlawful because it directly contravened Pācittiya 37 [Bapat 1956; Hazra 2002; Sarao & Long 2017; Entrance to the Vinaya 1983].
Curated parallels exist across virtually all surviving monastic codes, including the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Prātimokṣas and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Dharmaguptaka lineages preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, alongside the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 120) and the Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies a resembling parallel in the *Sattasatikakkhandhaka* (Kd 22), where the council proceedings are recounted [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus matches reflect heavy text reuse with other Theravāda Vinaya food regulations, sharing substantial material with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 38 (§1.20–2.3.2 ↔ §1.16–2.3.2), Pāṭidesanīya 1, Pācittiya 39, and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54, while showing cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122), and the *Prātimokṣasūtra* (D0002) [DharmaNexus].
